title: Durable Claude attempt dispatch
description: Objective: compose the real Claude launcher into a daemon/store-backed single-node work path so the canary does not orchestrate authority in test code. Deliverable: a daemon service and focused tests that durably claim exactly one low-risk execution-bearing node, commit attempt/effect/grant activation together, invoke the Windows Claude launch wrapper only after that commit, persist process registration/observations/result manifest, and recover duplicate/restart delivery without overlapping authority. NOT in scope: verification/review/final acceptance, multi-node/fan-out, MCP transport, or E2E fixtures. Depends on the Windows Claude launch wrapper task. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts/.js, foundation-attempt-service.ts/.js, and foundation-attempt-service.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A single authenticated request against a real SqliteEventStore claims one node and commits attempt/effect/grant activation atomically before the first physical launch; injected commit failure proves zero launch.

The service passes only the committed one-use grant and freshly observed runtime closure to @moe/runner's launcher and persists immutable process registration, raw evidence digests, and result-manifest identity.

Duplicate/replayed delivery leaves exactly one authoritative claim, one activation, and one process registration; it adopts or refuses before launch, asserted by raw durable row counts and launcher invocation count.
Unsupported graphs with more than one execution-bearing node refuse with a stable daemon code/layer and no claim/effect/resource/budget residue.
Crash/cancel/unknown launch outcomes persist honest SUSPECT/UNKNOWN or release facts and never silently relaunch; terminal/session events remain advisory and bind the current effect/session identity.
Runner, daemon, and repo-wide gates exit 0, and all production modules stay below 250 physical lines.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.note: createFoundationAttemptService + readFoundationAttemptRecord + exact one-line bridge landed. Order enforced: decode/snapshot request -> admitSingleExecutionNode over the PUBLIC validateGraphSnapshot -> seal the input manifest with bare-root buildInputManifest (the service owns the sealed manifest; the request only declares baseIdentity+entries, so no caller can hand in a pre-sealed one) -> decode the activation envelope for the admitted claim -> runEffectActivateCommand -> read the activation BACK from the store via readFoundationActivationHistory (never the caller's copy, never the command result) and check session + claim intentId/wrapperIdentity -> expected-version-0 reservation on the DERIVED, DISJOINT dispatch aggregate -> only a fresh DECIDED reservation launches. Every delegated refusal keeps its producer's code and refusedBy verbatim. Default path builds createFoundationClaudeLauncher over the activation aggregate and key; launchRequestBody passes the durable effect/attempt/UNUSED grant and admitted claim with priorRegistration and duplicateDelivery pinned null and no runtime observation of its own. Launch/capture are contained: a non-native thenable is never awaited, and the launch port must answer with a real promise. PROVEN only reaches the daemon-owned capture port, whose answer is exact-key checked before bare-root buildResultManifest seals it against the service's own input manifest. The final advisory record is appended at expected version 1 and then RE-READ, re-decoded and byte-compared — the caller's candidate is never echoed. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS STEP: contained() originally required a native promise for BOTH ports, which would have turned every synchronous capture answer into a false CAPTURE_UNKNOWN. implementationPlan.description: TDD recovery/concurrency hardening — add each case RED, then minimally refine the service. Gate the winning launch promise and issue concurrent identical deliveries: assert one activation, one dispatch reservation, one PROCESS_OBSERVED registration (PREFLIGHT is not process authority), one final record, exactly one launcher invocation, and one capture; the loser must adopt the byte-identical final durable record or return exact `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS`/SUSPECT before launch. Replay after completion must answer from stored bytes even when a caller candidate drifts; changed command/manifest/binding bytes must refuse without overwrite. Cover restart windows with reservation-only, grant-consumed-only, PREFLIGHT-only, PROCESS_OBSERVED-without-result, result-capture throw/malformed result, UNKNOWN/cancelled launch observation, and ambiguous final commit: persist or read an honest UNKNOWN/SUSPECT advisory bound to the current effect/session/process facts, never turn it into a result manifest, never feed pending registration back as prior, and never silently relaunch. Assert raw event-type and decision counts and exact code/layer for every refusal; generated crash cases must assert a positive case count.
implementationPlan.note: Recovery/concurrency cases landed and green. CONCURRENCY: the winning launch promise is gated, two identical deliveries are issued, and the assertions are exact counts — 1 launcher invocation, 1 capture, activation events exactly ["EffectActivationCommitted"], dispatch events exactly ["FoundationDispatchReserved","FoundationAttemptRecorded"], winner ok, loser refused FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT before any launch. REPLAY AFTER COMPLETION: the second delivery returns a digest and record STRICTLY EQUAL to the first with still exactly 1 launch and 1 capture, and the read model agrees — the answer comes from stored bytes, proven by drill 3 below. CAPTURE FAILURE: a throwing capture port yields FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_CAPTURE_UNKNOWN @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT, and the persisted record is an honest truthClass UNKNOWN with resultManifest null that still carries the PROCESS_OBSERVED processIdentity — an unusable result never becomes a result manifest. LAUNCH THROW: truthClass SUSPECT, resultManifest null, and a restart-shaped redelivery ADOPTS the stored record with the launch count still 1 — no silent relaunch. PLATFORM: the real runner's CLAUDE_LAUNCH_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED @ LAUNCHER is persisted as UNKNOWN and the activation aggregate has no tail, proving the grant was never consumed. ABSENT READ: FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT and FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_MALFORMED both pinned. SCOPE HONESTY: the plan also lists grant-consumed-only, PREFLIGHT-only and PROCESS_OBSERVED-without-result restart windows as separate cases. Those interior states live on the ACTIVATION aggregate and are owned/asserted by foundation-launch-authority.test.ts; from this service's seam they are all indistinguishable instances of the same fact — a reservation exists with no final record — which the DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS and adopt-after-throw cases cover directly. I did not fabricate separate cases that would only re-assert the launch authority's own tests.

REACHABLE FROM THE BARE ROOT `@moe/runner` (no deep import; the exports map is exclusive `{".": "./src/index.ts"}`):
  createClaudeLauncher(authority: unknown): (value: unknown, options?: ClaudeLaunchOptions) => Promise<ClaudeLaunchResult>

  type ClaudeLauncherAuthority, ClaudeRegistrationCommit, ClaudeLaunchRegistrationPhase
Proven by a real child-Node probe with `--experimental-strip-types`, cwd = packages/runner, resolving through the package's own self-reference:
  {"outcome":"RAN","factory":"function","phases":["PREFLIGHT","STARTED"],"defaultsWithheld":true,"kind":"REFUSED","code":"CLAUDE_LAUNCH_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED","layer":"LAUNCHER","truthClass":"UNSUPPORTED","grants":0,"regs":0}

AUTHORITY PORT SIGNATURES. Both return `unknown` on purpose — they cross a process boundary, so a declared return type would be a claim about your code. The launcher DECODES both before branching.
  consumeGrantDurably(grant: unknown, wrapperIdentity: unknown): unknown
  commitProcessRegistration(commit: ClaudeRegistrationCommit): unknown
  ClaudeRegistrationCommit = { readonly phase: "PREFLIGHT" | "STARTED"; readonly registration: LaunchLockRegistration; readonly claim: unknown; readonly prior: unknown }

WHAT THE LAUNCHER ACCEPTS BACK — exact shapes, anything else fails closed:
- consumeGrantDurably success: `{ kind: "CONSUMED", ok: true, grant, versionDelta: 1 }` where `grant` parses as an ActivationGrant with `state: "CONSUMED"`. `versionDelta` other than exactly 1 is MALFORMED.
- commitProcessRegistration success: `{ kind: "REGISTERED", ok: true, registration }` where `registration` parses as a LaunchLockRegistration.
- refusal from either: `{ kind: "REFUSED" | "SUSPECT", failure }` with `failure` a whole SupervisorFailure (ok:false, code in SUPERVISOR_ERROR_CODES, layer in SUPERVISOR_LAYERS, string message, exact `detail` = {state, command, leg}). Your code and layer are PRESERVED verbatim — that is how a durable replay surfaces as GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED at GRANT rather than as a generic launcher error.
- A throw, a Promise, a thenable, a Proxy, an accessor, a wrong `kind`, or a payload that does not re-parse all become CLAUDE_LAUNCH_DEPENDENCY_THROWN at GRANT / CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LOCK_UNKNOWN at LAUNCH_LOCK. NEVER return a Promise: these ports are called SYNCHRONOUSLY and an awaited value is not one. If your store is async, resolve it before you call the launcher.

PHASE CONTRACT — commitProcessRegistration is called EXACTLY TWICE per launch:
1. phase "PREFLIGHT", processIdentity `pending:<wrapperIdentity>`, BEFORE the OS-exclusive lock and BEFORE any physical open.
2. phase "STARTED", processIdentity `windows:<pid>:<creationTime>`, AFTER the boundary reports a started process.
Both strings are built by `pendingProcessIdentity` / `startedProcessIdentity` in claude-launcher-contract.ts, which are now the single source of truth for those formats. Refusing at PREFLIGHT is how you stop a second physical open for a lock that already carries a live process.

THE TRAP, and it is the one that will bite you: A DURABLE PENDING REGISTRATION MUST NEVER BE FED BACK AS `priorRegistration`. You may RESERVE at PREFLIGHT, but only the STARTED record is process authority. If you persist the `pending:` row and hand it back on the next launch, the PURE `registerLaunchLock` runs first and refuses LAUNCH_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_REUSED at LAUNCH_LOCK — the bootstrap credential digest matches — so a legitimate restart is refused instead of adopted. Adoption/restart decisions belong in your store, expressed through the PREFLIGHT commit's own refusal, not through `priorRegistration`.

TWO MORE FACTS YOU WILL NEED:
- The launcher DEEP-COPIES the request, so the `claim` travelling back out to your port is an EQUAL record, not the object you passed. Do not key anything on object identity.
- Capabilities are bound ONCE at `createClaudeLauncher` time. Mutating the authority object afterwards cannot redirect an in-flight launch. `this` is still your authority object, so a class instance reading its own fields works normally.
- A malformed authority does not throw: you get a launcher that refuses CLAUDE_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY_UNUSABLE at LAUNCHER without touching any port.
- Everything else is the SHIPPED default: runtime pin, duplicate resolver, Windows Job boundary, OS-exclusive lock, process observation, clock, delay. `CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_DEFAULTS` and the eight individual ports are deliberately NOT published, and index-surface.test.ts has a negative control asserting nine such names stay off the root. Do not reimplement them; you cannot reach them.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: runtime-to-activation binding — comparing the prepared runtime observation digest against `EffectIntent.runtimeObservationDigest` before grant/open — is NOT in this overlay and is NOT yours either. It is owned by sibling task-de496f4785a242569aa4ffc3ef6f1d69. Do not add that guard here or in your dispatcher.

Evidence for this seam: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` exit 0, 56 files / 1764 tests; repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` both exit 0 (249 files, 5437 passed, 1 skipped). Seven mutation drills confirm the delegation, the two phases, the pure-first composition, the shipped-defaults composition, the phase classifier and the option-forwarding paths are all load-bearing.
